tasks.short: Keep employee benefits and pension records correct, and sort out changes with providers.

today.trigger: An employee joins, leaves or changes circumstances, or a provider sends a statement or renewal.
steps: Check the employee's AFAS record, applicable CAO and benefit eligibility.
Collect required information and prepare changes for the provider.
Submit changes through the agreed provider channel and chase confirmation.
Reconcile provider statements against employee records and payroll deductions.
Explain cover, contributions or corrections to the employee and Payroll Specialist.
drudgery: Entering the same employee change twice
Matching provider statements to payroll records
today.time_sinks: Missing identifiers, conflicting effective dates and provider response times create repeated checking and follow-up.

lenses.faster: Compare AFAS changes with provider records automatically and prepare completed change files. Manual matching and most rekeying disappear.
lenses.autonomous: An approved AFAS change starts an eligibility check, prepares the provider submission and tracks acknowledgement. The specialist approves submissions and handles discrepancies.
lenses.ambitious: Reconcile every covered employee monthly and identify missed enrolments or incorrect contributions before employees discover them.
lenses.joy: Remove spreadsheet matching and routine chasing, leaving more time to explain benefits and resolve difficult provider cases.
lenses.options: Compare renewal options by employer cost, employee contribution, cover and administrative burden.
lenses.altitude: Own eligibility rules, reconciliation controls and provider service standards instead of processing each change manually.
reach: Prepare benefit-related payroll exceptions for the Payroll Specialist.
Provide reconciled contribution accrual inputs to the Controller.

tasks.human_edge: Interpret unusual eligibility cases, explain sensitive changes and negotiate with brokers or providers.
tasks.pattern_why: Provider administration spans records, submissions and acknowledgements; deterministic checks can prepare the work, but coverage and contribution changes need approval.

in_practice.trigger: A daily AFAS change extract arrives or a provider statement is received.
steps: Validate identifiers, effective dates and eligibility against approved scheme rules.
Reconcile changes and statements using deterministic calculations; extract unfamiliar document fields into a review queue.
Prepare a change file, discrepancy list and employee explanation with source references.
Present submissions and corrections for specialist approval.
Send approved changes through a supported channel and track acknowledgements.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves every provider submission and correction; Payroll approves payroll deductions through its existing controls.
systems: AFAS Profit approved export or connector
data_needed: Employment dates, hours and relevant salary components
Applicable CAO and approved scheme rules
Approved contribution tables and effective dates
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint benefits change register containing source versions, validation results, approvals and provider acknowledgements.

evidence.claim: Power Query can merge structured employee and provider tables to identify unmatched records.
The proposed workflow could reduce reconciliation and submission effort, subject to provider formats and access.

risks: An incorrect eligibility rule or effective date could cause missing cover or incorrect contributions.
Provider access and supported upload formats may prevent automated submission.
Benefit records can contain sensitive personal information; restrict access and avoid collecting medical details.
research_questions: Which schemes actually apply to each employee group, including pension obligations and any savings arrangement?
Can each provider supply stable identifiers, structured statements and submission acknowledgements?
How many hours currently go to reconciliation, submissions and waiting, and what error rate must a pilot improve?

tasks.short: Assess jobs against the right CAO and job evaluation framework, then recommend a grade and salary range.

today.trigger: A manager creates a role, changes its responsibilities or requests a grading review.
steps: Collect the job description and interview the manager or jobholder.
Establish the applicable CAO, working-time rules and job evaluation method.
Assess responsibilities and compare the position with established reference jobs.
Check salary scales, internal consistency and relevant market evidence.
Discuss and document the recommended classification and salary range.
systems: SharePoint job descriptions and CAO documents
drudgery: Checking scale versions and effective dates
today.time_sinks: Incomplete descriptions and disagreement about actual responsibilities lead to repeated interviews and comparisons.

lenses.faster: Extract responsibilities and retrieve comparable approved jobs with their evaluation evidence. The specialist starts with a structured assessment instead of a blank form.
lenses.autonomous: A grading request generates a completeness check, comparison pack and missing-information questions. Grade and pay recommendations remain with the specialist.
lenses.ambitious: Review comparable jobs across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo for inconsistent grading and unexplained differences.
lenses.joy: Spend less time searching documents and more time understanding what employees actually do.
lenses.options: Show plausible classifications with the evidence and unresolved questions for each, without treating model scores as objective measurements.
lenses.altitude: Maintain a consistent job architecture and assessment standard across the company.
reach: Help Recruiters establish approved vacancy salary ranges.
Support HR Business Partners with job design and progression criteria.

tasks.human_edge: Observe real work, challenge inflated descriptions and defend a fair assessment to managers and employees.
tasks.pattern_why: Document comparison and evidence preparation are suitable for assistance, while job evaluation and consequential pay recommendations require accountable judgment.

in_practice.trigger: A manager submits a job evaluation request with a description and reason for review.
steps: Check required information and identify the applicable evaluation framework.
Extract responsibilities with references to the submitted evidence.
Retrieve approved reference jobs and current CAO scales.
Draft a factor-by-factor comparison and flag unsupported assumptions.
Have the specialist complete the evaluation and route the recommendation for approval.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist determines the recommendation; the designated approver authorizes classification and pay changes before AFAS is updated.
systems: AFAS Profit read-only job and salary data
data_needed: Current job descriptions and interview evidence
Approved reference jobs and evaluation rationales
Current salary scales and effective dates
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint job evaluation register recording evidence, framework versions, specialist reasoning and approvals.

evidence.claim: A language model can structure job descriptions and draft comparisons against supplied criteria, subject to human verification.
SharePoint supports versioned document libraries for maintaining approved job descriptions and reference material.

risks: US exempt or non-exempt categories do not apply here; assess Dutch CAO coverage and relevant Dutch rules.
Descriptions and historical grades may encode bias or fail to reflect actual work.
Assess EU AI Act applicability before using AI to evaluate jobs or recommend remuneration; meaningful human review alone does not settle that assessment.
research_questions: Which evaluation methods and appeal procedures are binding under each CAO?
Are reference jobs supported by consistent, current assessment evidence?
Does a pilot improve assessment time and reviewer agreement without increasing unexplained grading differences?

tasks.short: Research benefit and workplace health practices, and recommend practical policy changes for our sites.

today.trigger: A renewal, employee concern, absence trend, legal change or management request prompts a policy review.
steps: Define the issue with HR Business Partners and the relevant safety or occupational-health lead.
Collect current policies, aggregated workforce evidence and authoritative external material.
Compare possible changes against CAO obligations, cost and employee needs.
Discuss feasibility with site managers, Finance and employee representatives as required.
Prepare a recommendation and an implementation and evaluation plan.
today.time_sinks: Separating credible guidance from supplier claims and establishing whether a practice suits shift workers.

lenses.faster: Prepare a source-linked evidence brief and policy comparison automatically. The specialist checks the evidence and tests local suitability.
lenses.autonomous: A scheduled review flags policy renewal dates and changes in selected authoritative sources, then prepares a review pack.
lenses.ambitious: Run small, evaluated policy pilots for shift workers and office staff instead of relying on a company-wide annual review.
lenses.joy: Replace document hunting with conversations about benefits people can actually use.
lenses.options: Compare several policy packages by cost, accessibility across shifts, likely uptake and strength of evidence.
lenses.altitude: Own a continuous policy evaluation process with explicit outcomes and review dates.
reach: Help People Analytics define benefit uptake and outcome measures.
Support Learning and Development with policy-related training needs identified by the safety lead.

tasks.human_edge: Judge employee needs, interpret weak evidence and negotiate workable changes with site leaders and representatives.
tasks.pattern_why: Research synthesis and option drafting can be accelerated, but policy choices depend on context, consultation and professional expertise.

in_practice.trigger: A policy review date arrives or an agreed workforce indicator crosses a review threshold.
steps: Collect approved policy versions, aggregated indicators and dated authoritative sources.
Draft a comparison separating legal requirements, research findings and supplier claims.
Calculate costs and identify groups that may have difficulty accessing each option.
Have the specialist and relevant safety or occupational-health professional review the proposal.
Route the chosen proposal through management and any required OR process, then define pilot measures.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist verifies recommendations; qualified professionals review health and safety content, and authorized leaders approve policy changes after required consultation or consent.
systems: Approved research and document analysis tools
data_needed: Current policies and applicable CAO provisions
Aggregated benefit uptake and absence indicators
Aggregated training and certificate completion data
Employee feedback across sites and shifts
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint policy evidence register with source dates, option assumptions, professional reviews and decisions.

evidence.claim: Power BI can present trends from prepared HR datasets for policy review.
Source-linked research drafting could reduce preparation time, but local policy effectiveness requires evaluation.

risks: Research findings may not transfer to warehouse, transport or night-shift work.
Small workforce groups can be identifiable even in aggregated reports; apply disclosure controls.
Keep medical assessment with the bedrijfsarts and occupational-health service; policy research must not become individual medical profiling.
research_questions: Which recurring policy reviews consume enough research effort to justify this workflow?
Can indicators be reported safely while still revealing differences between sites and shifts?
Which pilot outcomes would demonstrate benefit, and which decisions require OR consent or other formal involvement?

tasks.short: Explain Dutch employment rules, CAO provisions and our pay and benefits policies to managers and employees.

today.trigger: An employee or manager asks about pay, allowances, benefits, procedures or job classification.
steps: Clarify the question and collect the relevant employment facts.
Identify the applicable CAO, contract terms and current policy versions.
Check provisions and calculations, consulting Payroll or an HR Business Partner where needed.
Explain the answer, its basis and any unresolved issue.
Record the advice and arrange any authorized follow-up.
drudgery: Answering repeated allowance and benefit questions
today.time_sinks: Questions arrive without the employee group, working pattern or effective date needed to give a reliable answer.

lenses.faster: Retrieve applicable clauses and draft a plain-English answer with references. The specialist spends time on interpretation and the conversation.
lenses.autonomous: Incoming questions receive a topic classification and a draft request for missing facts; approved general FAQs can be displayed automatically.
lenses.ambitious: Make reliable guidance available across shifts and use recurring questions to improve policies and onboarding.
lenses.joy: Reduce repeated searching while preserving the conversations where reassurance or careful explanation matters.
lenses.options: Prepare a short employee explanation, a detailed manager briefing and alternative interpretations where the rules are unclear.
lenses.altitude: Own an approved advice library, escalation rules and quality checks instead of recreating each answer.
reach: Maintain pay and benefits onboarding guidance for HR Administrators.
Support HR Business Partners with consistent manager briefings.

tasks.human_edge: Recognize sensitive circumstances, explain difficult outcomes and take responsibility for interpretation.
tasks.pattern_why: Retrieval and drafting are checkable support steps; personalized advice can affect rights and income and stays with the specialist.

in_practice.trigger: A question is submitted through an agreed HR mailbox or intake form.
steps: Identify the topic and check that necessary employment facts are available.
Retrieve only authorized, effective CAO, contract and policy material.
Draft an answer with exact references, assumptions and escalation flags.
Have the specialist verify the interpretation and any calculation before sending.
Record the final advice and propose an anonymized FAQ update where useful.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves personalized advice; disputed legal interpretations go to the appropriate HR lead or legal adviser.
data_needed: The question and minimum necessary employment facts
Current approved policies and effective dates
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted HR advice register linking the final answer to its sources, reviewer and any follow-up.

evidence.claim: SharePoint provides permission-controlled document storage and version history for approved guidance.
Retrieval-assisted drafting can speed up repeated policy questions when reviewers verify applicability and citations.

risks: A correct quotation from the wrong CAO or policy version can produce incorrect advice.
Confident drafting can hide missing facts or conflicting provisions.
Absence questions must respect Wet verbetering poortwachter responsibilities and exclude unnecessary medical information.
research_questions: What proportion of questions repeat, and how much time goes to searching versus interpreting?
Can every answer source be assigned an owner, effective date and employee scope?
Does a reviewed pilot reduce response time while maintaining accuracy on ambiguous and cross-CAO questions?

tasks.short: Design and run salary review and incentive arrangements within our CAOs and approved budget.

today.trigger: An annual salary review, CAO change or proposed incentive arrangement requires design or administration.
steps: Confirm mandatory increases, policy objectives, budget and employee eligibility.
Assemble salary, grade, hours and relevant award inputs.
Model allocations and check scale limits, fairness and employer costs.
Discuss proposals with managers, Finance and the HR Director, involving the OR where required.
Obtain approval, prepare payroll instructions and reconcile implementation.
drudgery: Recalculating budget totals after every revision
Checking awards against scales and eligibility rules
today.time_sinks: Repeated allocation changes, inconsistent inputs and reconciliation between approved awards and payroll.

lenses.faster: Use a controlled calculation model to validate inputs, calculate costs and prepare payroll instructions. Spreadsheet consolidation and repeated manual checks disappear.
lenses.autonomous: An approved review calendar starts data preparation and validation; manager submissions automatically update a draft budget and exception list.
lenses.ambitious: Check every proposed award for scale compliance, affordability and unexplained differences before approval.
lenses.joy: Spend less time repairing workbooks and more time designing rewards managers and employees understand.
lenses.options: Compare general increases, targeted adjustments and incentive designs under the same budget, with employee and employer effects shown separately.
lenses.altitude: Own compensation rules, decision controls and outcome evaluation across each review cycle.
reach: Prepare personnel-cost scenarios with FP&A.
Provide validated salary-change batches to the Payroll Specialist.

tasks.human_edge: Set reward objectives, challenge manager recommendations and balance fairness, affordability and workforce trust.
tasks.pattern_why: Deterministic calculations can administer approved rules, while multi-party decisions and pay changes require explicit authorization.

in_practice.trigger: The HR Director authorizes a compensation review with a budget and approved rules.
steps: Create a dated AFAS snapshot and validate grades, hours, salary components and eligibility.
Calculate mandatory changes and model discretionary scenarios separately.
Collect authorized manager proposals and flag rule breaches or unexplained differences.
Present the proposed awards, total employer cost and exceptions for approval.
Prepare an approved payroll change file and reconcile it against Payroll's test calculation.
in_practice.human_gate: The HR Director and budget owner approve awards and exceptions; Payroll validates and executes pay changes under existing controls.
data_needed: Salary components, grades, hours and employment dates
Applicable CAO scales and mandatory increases
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted compensation-cycle register containing input snapshots, calculation versions, proposals, approvals and payroll reconciliation.

evidence.claim: Excel supports repeatable compensation calculations and what-if analysis using explicit assumptions.
Automated validation and reconciliation could reduce compensation-cycle administration; the saving is untested here.

risks: Incorrect salary-component or pension assumptions can materially understate employer cost.
Incentives could encourage unsafe speed, excessive hours or attending work while unwell.
Check required OR involvement and CAO constraints; assess EU AI Act obligations if AI influences individual award recommendations.
research_questions: Which awards are mandatory, discretionary or constrained by each CAO?
Can the model reproduce a completed review and payroll outcome within agreed tolerances?
Which decisions require management approval, OR involvement or collective bargaining before implementation?

tasks.short: Investigate pay and grading complaints, and advise on a fair resolution.

today.trigger: An employee, manager or HR Business Partner raises a salary or classification complaint.
steps: Hear the concern and record the requested outcome.
Collect the relevant job, pay, CAO and previous decision evidence.
Reconstruct the classification or pay calculation and identify disputed facts.
Discuss findings and possible remedies with the appropriate HR and management stakeholders.
Advise on resolution, communicate the reasoning and track any correction or appeal.
drudgery: Rechecking historical scales and salary calculations
today.time_sinks: Missing decision records, disputed descriptions of actual work and the time needed to establish trust.

lenses.faster: Build a referenced chronology and reproduce the relevant calculations before the specialist reviews the case.
lenses.autonomous: A registered complaint creates an evidence checklist, deadline reminders and a draft case pack. Findings and advice require human review.
lenses.ambitious: Use anonymized complaint patterns to identify inconsistent grading or recurring allowance errors across sites.
lenses.joy: Remove document chasing so the specialist can listen carefully and explain the outcome.
lenses.options: Prepare several supported remedies, including correction, further job evaluation or formal appeal, with their costs and procedural requirements.
lenses.altitude: Improve the fairness and traceability of the complaint process rather than rebuilding each case from scratch.
reach: Prepare evidence packs for HR Business Partners handling employee relations.
Refer verified recurring calculation defects to Payroll and the HRIS Analyst.

tasks.human_edge: Hear the employee, assess conflicting accounts, recognize unequal treatment and give advice people can challenge.
tasks.pattern_why: Despite the earlier automate label, complaint advice depends on contested facts, employee trust and accountable judgment; evidence preparation is the suitable automation target.

in_practice.trigger: A complaint is formally registered through the agreed HR process.
steps: Record the concern, applicable procedure and deadlines without predicting the outcome.
Collect authorized evidence and construct a chronology with source references.
Recalculate disputed amounts deterministically and flag missing or contradictory facts.
Draft findings and remedy options for specialist investigation and discussion.
Record the human-approved advice and track correction or appeal milestones.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist verifies facts and gives advice; the designated decision-maker authorizes remedies, and the employee retains the applicable appeal route.
data_needed: Historical salary records and applicable scales
in_practice.logs_to: The restricted employee-relations case register, with evidence references, calculation versions, human findings and appeal status.

evidence.claim: Document analysis can help draft a chronology from supplied correspondence, but completeness and interpretation need checking.
Nearly autonomous complaint resolution is not established by the supplied task score or company information.

risks: An incomplete case pack could make a defensible complaint appear unsupported.
Historical decisions may contain discriminatory practices that should not become precedents.
Broad search access could expose other employees' salaries or confidential complaints.
research_questions: How much case time is evidence preparation compared with interviews, deliberation and waiting?
Are historical grading decisions and appeal procedures sufficiently documented?
Can reviewers detect omitted or contradictory evidence reliably in a pilot using closed cases?

tasks.short: Maintain clear job descriptions, job classifications and current salary scales.

today.trigger: A role changes, a vacancy opens, a CAO scale changes or a scheduled job-library review is due.
steps: Collect the approved role requirements and current job evaluation outcome.
Draft or revise the description using the appropriate company template.
Check classification, salary scale, working pattern and consistency with comparable roles.
Obtain manager and specialist approval, including required governance steps.
Publish the approved version and update relevant HR and recruitment records.
drudgery: Checking whether different systems contain the same version
today.time_sinks: Unclear ownership and uncontrolled copies create repeated edits and conflicting descriptions.

lenses.faster: Draft descriptions from approved role facts and generate salary tables from verified scale data. Formatting and repetitive cross-checking largely disappear.
lenses.autonomous: An approved scale update identifies affected documents and prepares revisions; a role-change request starts a description draft.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain a current job library linking each role to progression requirements, vacancy content and approved training needs.
lenses.joy: Replace document maintenance with clearer conversations about responsibilities and career growth.
lenses.options: Create concise employee, detailed manager and recruitment versions from the same approved role facts.
lenses.altitude: Own the job-content standard and publication controls across HR systems.
reach: Provide approved role content to Recruiters.
Supply validated role and certificate requirements to Learning and Development.

tasks.human_edge: Confirm that descriptions reflect real work and distinguish essential requirements from preferences.
tasks.pattern_why: Drafting and consistency checks can run across documents and systems, but classification, requirements and publication need approval.

in_practice.trigger: An authorized role-change request or verified CAO scale update enters the maintenance queue.
steps: Retrieve the approved role facts, evaluation outcome and effective scale version.
Draft description changes and calculate scale tables using explicit rules.
Check required fields, cross-document consistency and unsupported requirements.
Present a change comparison for manager and specialist approval.
Publish approved documents and route controlled updates to AFAS and Recruitee owners.
in_practice.human_gate: The manager confirms actual responsibilities and the specialist approves classification and scale references before publication or system updates.
data_needed: Applicable salary scales and effective dates
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint job-library change register with source facts, document differences, approvals and publication versions.

evidence.claim: Word templates and SharePoint version history support standardized, controlled job-description maintenance.
Drafting from approved facts could reduce maintenance effort, provided invented responsibilities are rejected during review.

risks: Generated descriptions may invent duties, qualifications or certificate requirements.
A scale update could be applied to the wrong CAO group or effective date.
Updating recruitment text without the approved job record could create inconsistent promises to candidates.
research_questions: How many distinct jobs and uncontrolled description copies currently exist?
Is there an agreed owner and approved evaluation outcome for each role?
Can a pilot propagate one verified scale change accurately across all affected documents and system handoffs?

tasks.short: Calculate the cost and workforce effects of CAO and compensation proposals.

today.trigger: Management needs a bargaining position, a CAO proposal must be costed or Finance requests a workforce-cost scenario.
steps: Agree the proposal, comparison baseline, time horizon and workforce scope.
Collect payroll, headcount, hours, allowance and relevant flex-worker cost inputs.
Build calculations for salary changes, employer charges and workforce assumptions.
Compare scenarios and reconcile the baseline with Payroll and Finance.
Explain cost drivers, uncertainties and distributional effects to decision-makers.
systems: AFAS Profit payroll and general ledger
drudgery: Tracing differences between HR and Finance totals
today.time_sinks: Unreconciled baselines and hidden assumptions about allowances, employer contributions and flex-worker costs.

lenses.faster: Run proposals through a reusable, reconciled cost model. Repeated joins and workbook rebuilding disappear.
lenses.autonomous: A refreshed data snapshot or new scenario request runs validation and recalculation, then prepares an exceptions and results pack.
lenses.ambitious: Cost more bargaining options and show their effects by site, employee group and pay band before choosing a position.
lenses.joy: Spend less time repairing formulas and more time explaining which assumptions change the decision.
lenses.options: Compare percentage increases, fixed amounts, allowance changes and phased dates with sensitivity ranges for staffing and uptake.
lenses.altitude: Own a transparent workforce-cost model and its assumptions, reconciliations and uncertainty limits.
reach: Support FP&A with personnel-cost forecasts and sensitivities.
Help the Controller explain payroll-related budget variances.

tasks.human_edge: Choose credible assumptions, interpret bargaining trade-offs and explain uncertainty without false precision.
tasks.pattern_why: Use deterministic software for calculations and reconciliation, with a human gate before a multi-step analysis becomes an official bargaining or budget input.

in_practice.trigger: An authorized user submits a scenario against an agreed, dated workforce baseline.
steps: Load approved AFAS and relevant agency extracts and reconcile baseline totals with Finance.
Translate the proposal into explicit parameters, with specialist review of ambiguous wording.
Calculate direct pay, applicable employer costs and timing effects using versioned rules.
Run validation and sensitivity checks and prepare aggregate comparisons.
Have the specialist and Finance approve the figures before circulation.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist validates proposal interpretation and Finance approves baseline reconciliation and costing assumptions before figures are used in negotiations or budgets.
systems: Excel Power Query and controlled calculation model
data_needed: Salary components, contracted hours and allowance drivers
Applicable employer contribution and pension rules
General ledger control totals and relevant agency rates
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint scenario register containing baseline identifiers, parameter sets, calculation versions, reconciliations and approvals.

evidence.claim: Power Query can combine structured extracts, and Excel supports parameterized what-if calculations.
evidence.source: Microsoft Excel Power Query; Microsoft Excel

evidence.claim: A reusable reconciled model could shorten successive bargaining analyses; savings depend on baseline quality and proposal complexity.

risks: Omitting pension effects, allowance interactions or implementation timing can understate costs.
The nightly Power BI extract may lag payroll corrections; every analysis needs a stated snapshot date.
Agency costs and obligations cannot be inferred directly from employee salary increases; validate contract terms separately.
research_questions: Can the baseline reconcile to payroll and general ledger totals with explained differences?
Which proposal interactions materially affect employer cost, including pension, allowances and effective dates?
Can the model reproduce a previous negotiated change and its realized cost within agreed tolerances?
Who may see bargaining scenarios, and which aggregate breakdowns remain confidential?

role.altitude: Become the owner of fair, understandable pay and benefits systems: maintain the rules, test the controls and help leaders make defensible workforce decisions.
reach: Prepare reconciled benefit and salary-change inputs for Payroll.
Co-own personnel-cost scenarios with FP&A and the Controller.
Maintain approved vacancy salary ranges and job content for Recruiters.
Support HR Business Partners with grading evidence, complaint preparation and manager guidance.
Define compensation data-quality checks with the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst.
role.ceiling_note: These eight tasks cover 870.6 hours, about 54% of a 1,600-hour role year. The unvalidated estimates imply roughly 389 hours of annual specialist capacity, worth about EUR 29,200 at EUR 75/hour, before setup and maintenance. This is capacity value, not a cash saving. Time-saved percentages concern specialist effort; speedups estimate elapsed task completion including review and external waits. Provider responses, consultation, appeals and approval cycles limit elapsed gains. Payroll authorization, medical judgments and bargaining mandates stay with their accountable owners.
skills_to_grow: Translate CAO and benefit provisions into testable rules with effective dates.
Build and reconcile controlled Excel and Power Query models.
Evaluate AI drafts for unsupported claims, bias and missing evidence.
Design permissions, retention and audit records consistent with AVG/GDPR.
Assess intended AI uses with legal and privacy colleagues, including EU AI Act employment provisions where applicable.
Explain pay trade-offs and work with the OR on applicable remuneration, job evaluation and benefit-system changes.
role.ambitious_version: Run a dependable pay and benefits service across all three sites: detect missed benefits, maintain consistent job architecture, test compensation options quickly and explain decisions clearly to shift and office workers. Link approved salary ranges and benefit guidance to recruitment and onboarding, then test whether clearer expectations and fewer pay errors improve offer acceptance, manager satisfaction and 90-day retention.
